answer: An inspector opens a hive with smoke and a steady hand, then writes the brood, the queen, the stores, the date. Proof of apiary inspector certification via beekeepers association reads like that notebook: a certification the beekeepers have renewed after every hive inspection season. One invented inspection costs a pencil. Fifty invented inspections cost fifty hives, fifty queens the inspector never saw, and the tide of each is the sting on his glove — the juniper is the beekeeper who stood beside him, the spiral the smoker, cold now and smelling of pine.
